tasks.title: Essay: Museum access priorities
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write 140–190 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: In your English class you have been talking about how to make museums more inclusive. Now your English teacher has asked you to write an essay.

promptBlocks.heading: Notes
paragraphs: 2. guided tours for visitors with disabilities

promptBlocks.text: Write an essay using all the notes and giving reasons for your point of view.

tasks.title: Review: Museum inclusion programme
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 140–190 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.heading: Reviews wanted!
paragraphs: Have you visited a museum that has introduced an inclusion programme – for example, sensory-friendly hours, multilingual guides, or free entry for certain groups?
Write a review for a specialist magazine about museums.
Describe what the programme involved, say how effective it was for visitors, and recommend one improvement the museum could make.
The best reviews will be published in the next issue.

tasks.title: Article: Involving the community
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 140–190 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted!
paragraphs: Our town museum wants to attract more local residents. What could it do to become a more welcoming place for everyone?
Write an article for the museum's website suggesting one practical change the museum could make, explaining why it would work and what the benefits would be for the community.
We will publish the best articles on our website.

tasks.title: Email: Museum visit arrangements
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 140–190 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.subject: Museum visit next month
paragraphs: I'm planning to visit your town next month and I'd love to go to the local museum. I've heard it has a new inclusion programme. Can you tell me what the programme involves? Also, do you think it's worth visiting? And could you recommend one exhibit I shouldn't miss?

designReview.overallOriginalityCheck: All tasks are based on the specific setting 'a museum inclusion programme planning brief 11' as required. No reused scenarios, audiences, content points, or sentence skeletons from previous tests. Forbidden concepts (e.g., peer learning, touring holiday, environment essay) are avoided. Each task has a concrete audience, clear communicative purpose, and at least two distinct content points. The essay uses the standard FCE essay-notes template with two supplied notes plus own idea. The review and article use announcement panels with unique headings. The email uses an email block with a specific subject and sender. All prompts are original and level-appropriate.

tasks.scenario: Museum inclusion programme planning brief 11: essay brief 1-1
tasks.purpose: Evaluate and justify priorities for museum inclusion (free admission days vs. guided tours for visitors with disabilities vs. own idea)
requiredContentPoints: guided tours for visitors with disabilities
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Scenario is unique to this test. Essay topic is about museum inclusion, not generic 'environment' or 'education'. No overlap with previous essay topics.

tasks.scenario: Museum inclusion programme planning brief 11: review brief 2-5
tasks.purpose: Assess effectiveness of a museum inclusion programme and recommend an improvement
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Review genre with a specific focus on museum inclusion programmes. Not a generic book/film/restaurant review. No overlap with previous review tasks.

tasks.scenario: Museum inclusion programme planning brief 11: article brief 3-9
tasks.purpose: Analyse implications and propose action to attract more local residents
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Article about making a museum more welcoming for locals. Not a generic 'learning beyond lessons' or 'most useful thing' article. No overlap with previous article tasks.

tasks.scenario: Museum inclusion programme planning brief 11: email brief 4-13
tasks.purpose: Explain a position and request arrangements for a museum visit
requiredContentPoints: opinion on whether it's worth visiting
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Email from a friend asking about a museum's inclusion programme. Not a generic 'touring holiday' or 'weekend job' email. No overlap with previous email tasks.
